gaps.sentence: He had hardly stepped off the plane ___ he was rushed into a meeting.
They behaved ___ nothing at all had happened.
gaps.explanation: 'As if + past perfect' signals that the comparison is contrary to fact.

gaps.sentence: Sales fell sharply last quarter; ___, the board cut the dividend.
gaps.explanation: The fall in sales caused the cut: as a result marks the consequence.

gaps.sentence: He didn't whisper the news; ___, he announced it to the whole office.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' corrects the first statement with its opposite.

gaps.sentence: British houses usually have gardens, ___ flats in Spain often have balconies.
She has decided to cycle to work ___ taking the bus.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' = in place of the bus journey.

gaps.sentence: The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: We went for a long walk ___ it was drizzling.
gaps.explanation: Only the conjunction 'even though' can introduce the finite clause 'it was drizzling'.
